claim_boundary: The local HTTP child lifecycle for Llama and MLX has one implementation for endpoint, log-tail, readiness, and teardown. Provider command construction, spawn semantics, and completion parsing remain provider-owned.
result_commit_ref: HEAD: the commit containing this receipt

canonical_owner.contract: A local HTTP child has an optional port, optional attached process, optional recorded detached PID plus start token, health-based readiness, readable-or-empty log access, and idempotent fail-closed cleanup.

scope.necessary_transport_adapter: hcli.serve._stop_owned_backend_children is a serving-process boundary cleanup adapter. It delegates only after checking the recorded process incarnation and does not implement a second lifecycle.

process_identity_contract.destructive_rule: Only matches may reach terminate_pid through detached fallback cleanup.
process_identity_contract.persistence_rule: RuntimePool retains the original recorded start token for a verified-but-unreaped or identity-unreadable child. A PID-reuse mismatch is reported as skipped and is not persisted as owned.

diff_ledger.interpretation: The duplicate backend bodies were deleted, but the tranche is not a net source reduction: it adds an explicit PID-incarnation safety contract, runtime/serve enforcement, and independent conformance coverage. Tests were retained rather than removed to improve this ledger.

known_baseline_failure.scope_relation: Unchanged by this tranche; it was reproduced on both base and measurement commits and is not counted as a lifecycle regression.

runtime_probe.purpose: Detect a gross direct-dispatch regression in the shared endpoint method without launching a provider.
runtime_probe.method: 41 samples of 20,000 LlamaServerBackend.endpoint calls in a fresh Python process; perf_counter_ns divided by calls per sample.
runtime_probe.result: No direct-dispatch regression observed in this run.
runtime_probe.limitations: This is a nanosecond-scale synthetic Python dispatch probe, run sequentially with uncontrolled CPU/cache state. It did not launch a model, HTTP provider, GPU, ANE, hawkingd, or Web process, so it is not a real serving-performance claim.

remaining_duplicate_authority: OpenAI/native and other non-local HTTP transports retain distinct lifecycle semantics outside this tranche.
Llama and MLX retain provider-specific spawn, command, and completion behavior because their semantics differ.
Resolved action identity remains the next authority boundary: the current selection path can still lose revision/grant/action information across Rust, Python, serve, and Web.
limitations: No real provider was launched, by the active Flash-lane isolation constraint.
This tranche proves one lifecycle owner for the three local backend classes; it does not claim all serving policy is unified.
The system-wide LOC ledger increased, so no repository-size reduction is claimed from this tranche alone.
